lit.'<p><b>R₀</b> es el número de personas q:
'

R₀ is the number of people each infected person infects, on average, in a population with no immunity: ≈ 1–2 for flu, ≈ 3–6 for the original SARS-CoV-2 and ≈ 12–18 for measles. If the effective number R > 1, cases rise; if R < 1, they fall. Ventilation, masks and fewer contacts lower R.

'
lit.'<p>Al inicio casi todos son <b>suscepti:
'

At first almost everyone is susceptible (S) and cases grow fast. The infected (I) are contagious for a few days and then recover (R) with immunity. As fewer susceptibles remain, each sick person infects fewer people: the curve reaches a peak and falls. This is the SIR model, used in public health.

'
lit.'<p>El cuerpo se defiende en capas: <b>b:
'

The body defends itself in layers: barriers (skin, mucous membranes, tears, stomach acid); the innate response, fast and non-specific (inflammation, fever, phagocytes); and the adaptive response, specific, with B lymphocytes that make antibodies and T lymphocytes. The latter creates memory: on a second infection it responds faster and more strongly. That is why the recovered (green) are not reinfected in this simulation.

'
lit.'<p>Las enfermedades infecciosas las cau:
'

Infectious diseases are caused by pathogens: viruses, bacteria, fungi or parasites. They are transmitted by direct contact, droplets and aerosols when coughing or talking, surfaces, contaminated water or food, or vectors such as mosquitoes. Here, each figure is a person: blue = susceptible, red = infected.

'
lit.'<p>Si una fracción suficiente de la pob:
'

If a large enough share of the population is immune, each infected person meets few susceptibles and R drops below 1: the epidemic does not take off and those who cannot be vaccinated (newborns, the immunocompromised) are protected too. The threshold is 1 − 1/R₀: ≈ 67 % for R₀ = 3 and ≈ 93 % for measles. Compare the size of the epidemic by coverage in the graph.

'
lit.'<p>Una <b>vacuna</b> presenta al sistem:
'

A vaccine shows the immune system an antigen from the pathogen (inactivated, weakened, a protein or its mRNA) so that it makes antibodies and memory without getting ill. Vaccinated people (yellow) are protected in ≈ 90 % of cases. Vaccines have eradicated smallpox and nearly eliminated polio and measles in many countries.

'
